verified: An arXiv preprint (2611.18330) by the Marimba authors describes a speech interface built on frozen Qwen3-ASR 0.6B features, where lexical term questions are scored zero-shot from ASR transcripts and non-lexical questions use a question-conditioned head plus a separate layer-18 turn-end readout; the author also links Apache-2.0 weights, code and a demo.
unconfirmed: All benchmark figures — matching or beating Qwen3-Omni (30B-A3B) on 6 of 9 tests, 100% language ID on 300 FLEURS clips, speaker-change AUROC of 0.966–0.980 on AMI and VoxConverse, and speaker count beating pyannote 3.1 — are author-reported in a non-peer-reviewed preprint with no independent replication; the authors themselves flag that the turn-end readout was trained on Smart Turn data and that all heads fall to chance on unseen CochlScene classification.

verified: 据 arXiv 论文（2611.18330）与作者帖，Marimba 以冻结的 Qwen3-ASR 0.6B 编码器特征为基础，每个音频窗口只跑一次编码；词汇类问题对 ASR 转写做零样本打分并做 Platt 校准，非词汇类问题用问题条件化读出头，turn-end 另用第 18 层读出；代码与 Apache-2.0 权重已公开。
unconfirmed: 论文自报的“9 项测试中 6 项追平或超过 Qwen3-Omni（30B-A3B）”、语言识别在 300 条 FLEURS 上 100%、说话人变化 AUROC 0.966–0.980、说话人计数优于 pyannote 3.1 等结果尚无第三方复现；作者也承认 turn-end 读出在 Smart Turn 数据上训练，该行仅对自家分布内有效，且在 CochlScene 等未见任务上各读出头仅达随机水平。
